source.title: Safeguard Fine-Tuned LLMs Through Pre- and Post-Tuning Model Merging
source.authors: Hua Farn; Hsuan Su; Shachi H. Kumar; Saurav Sahay; Shang-Tse Chen; Hung-yi Lee

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning of aligned models increases harmful compliance, using downstream-task SFT and harmful-response ASR; the settings and evaluation implementation differ from the original fine-tuning study.
record.gate_note: The study tests benign downstream-task fine-tuning against harmful prompts. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, token-position KL, compliant-prefix or jailbreak bypasses, safety localization in weights, or safety-deepening training. Results for merging methods are not cataloged as separate rows because merging is not one of the listed claim versions; table values for SFT are recorded.
record.test_reason: Table 1 reports harmful-prompt ASR (AdvBench, HEx-PHI; WildGuard judge) for three instruct models before and after LoRA SFT on four benign downstream tasks. This bears directly on V2, using a different recipe and judge from the original fine-tuning study. Merging is the paper's own mitigation and is not a deepening method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that benign downstream LoRA SFT degrades safety (which they frame as catastrophic forgetting), and that linearly merging the aligned and fine-tuned weights restores safety near aligned levels while keeping task gains, without safety data. They add that degradation is not consistently size-dependent and that categories 7 (Fraud/Deception) and 9 (Political Campaigning) are especially vulnerable.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign downstream-task SFT of aligned models and measures harmful-response ASR, but uses LoRA task fine-tuning, multiple tasks and model families, and WildGuard classification; it then studies model merging as a mitigation.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model family, downstream task, and safety benchmark; the paper also reports different fine-tuning steps for Tool Using Proficiency versus the other tasks.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, 2024
record.problems: Safety is evaluated with an automatic classifier rather than human-aligned evaluation; the authors note possible false positives and false negatives and coarse-grained outputs. ASR is averaged across three seeds, but no error bars or confidence intervals are provided. Jailbreak strategies are not evaluated, as the paper states.
record.rows_left_out: Not cataloged: numerical results for model merging, Dropout, Weight Decay, SLERP, and DARE in Table 1 and figures, because these interventions compare the paper's safety-restoration methods rather than test the listed claim versions. Downstream-task performance and IFEval results are also outside the listed versions.

untested.parts: Only LoRA (r=8) on four task datasets with fixed step counts. No identity-shifting or Alpaca/Dolly data, no full fine-tuning, no carefully selected benign data.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks; the paper explicitly excludes jailbreaks.
No localization of safety in weights or ranks.
The paper attributes degradation to catastrophic forgetting but does not test it.
No training that deepens safety; merging is a weight-interpolation mitigation.

missing.what: Average ASR change after SFT across model sizes. Smaller Qwen models degrade more, while larger Gemma is more affected; the authors say degradation is not determined by size alone.
AdvBench and HEx-PHI Pareto plots of SFT versus the aligned model. The text says SFT gives higher ASR in all settings, which conflicts with Table 1 for Gemma Reasoning.

record.verdict_notes: Uncertainty is not reported, and ASR is averaged over 3 seeds; changes of about 1 point equal a handful of prompts, so small rises or drops are treated as absent. WildGuard is the judge. The degradation is largest for LLaMA on Medical and Reasoning and weak or absent for Gemma-2-2B and most Qwen conditions, so V2's effect depends strongly on model and task. Merging, Dropout and Weight Decay rows were correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples is reported.
Tests benign downstream-task SFT, not every ordinary or carefully selected benign dataset or fine-tuning recipe.
No per-token KL divergence or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefill, suffix attack, or decoding-change bypass test; the paper explicitly excludes jailbreak-style attacks.
No test of whether safety is carried by a small set of weights or ranks.
Does not test why safety degradation occurs or whether the training data or objective causes shallowness.
Model merging is evaluated as a mitigation, but the study does not train safety to extend beyond initial response tokens or test whether such deepening holds up.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: SFT on downstream-task data; HEx-PHI harmful-response counts described by category before and after fine-tuning.
rows.baseline: Aligned model has harmful responses only in categories 4 (Malware), 9 (Political Campaigning), and 10 (Privacy Violation Activity).
rows.value: After fine-tuning, harmful responses increase across all categories; categories 4, 7 (Fraud/Deception), and 9 show the most significant growth in both tasks.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The text describes this pattern, but provides no category-specific numerical values.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: SFT on downstream-task data; HEx-PHI harmful-response counts described by category before and after fine-tuning.
rows.baseline: The aligned model generates harmful responses across more categories than LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct.
rows.value: Fine-tuning further aggravates the harmful-response issues; categories 7 and 9 have a large number of harmful responses across both models.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The text describes this pattern, but provides no category-specific numerical values.

relationships.condition: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct on Reasoning, Medical and Code; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on Reasoning; HEx-PHI category analysis
relationships.reason: ASR rises clearly after benign SFT, e.g. Medical 0→30.06% AdvBench and 1.22→38.85% HEx-PHI; Qwen Reasoning HEx-PHI 9.09→17.88% (r1-r6, r17, r18, r25, r26).
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose clearly after benign SFT, for example Medical from 0 to 30.06% on AdvBench and from 1.22 to 38.85% on HEx-PHI, and Qwen Reasoning from 9.09 to 17.88% on HEx-PHI.

relationships.condition: LLaMA Tool Using; Gemma-2-2B-It Reasoning HEx-PHI, Medical and Code; Qwen Medical HEx-PHI
relationships.reason: ASR rises only by small absolute amounts, mostly under 3 points; Gemma Code HEx-PHI reaches only 5.76% (r7, r8, r10-r14, r20).
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose only by small absolute amounts, mostly under 3 points; Gemma Code on HEx-PHI reached only 5.76%.

relationships.condition: Gemma Reasoning/AdvBench and Tool Using (both benchmarks); Qwen AdvBench for Medical, Code and Tool; Qwen HEx-PHI for Code and Tool
relationships.reason: Table 1 SFT ASR equals or falls below the aligned model, with changes of about 1 point or less (r9, r15, r16, r19, r21-r24).
relationships.display_finding: SFT ASR equalled or fell below the aligned model, with changes of about 1 point or less.
